messages.subject: Simulating leaf temperature in NicheMapR (microclimate and ectotherm parameters)
messages.subject_clean: Simulating leaf temperature in NicheMapR (microclimate and ectotherm parameters)
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mike,

I am using NicheMapR to simulate leaf temperature at a specific location over summer months of 2022-2023.

I have a few uncertainties regarding the input parameters:

1. For the microclimate model (micro_era5), I can't seem to increase the leaf height (Usrhyt) greater than 2 m. It appears I can't have a leaf height greater than the reference height (Refhy default = 2m). I would like to simulate a leaf on a tree - is it possible to  increase the height of the leaf beyond 2m? Say 5m.

2. For the ectotherm model, I am uncertain how to parametise the shape / size of the leaf using the proportionality factor (see below). I am guessing that for an leaf being an ellipsoid: b axis = length of the leaf surface, a axis = width of the leaf surface and c axis = thickness of leaf. But I am very unsure whether I have mixed up the a and b axis.

shape_b = 3, Proportionality factor (-) for going from volume to area, represents ratio of width:height for a plate, length:diameter for cylinder, b axis:a axis for ellipsoid

shape_c = 0.6666666667, Proportionality factor (-) for going from volume to area, represents ratio of length:height for a plate, c axis:a axis for ellipsoid

Any advice would be much appreciated.

Thanks :)
Lisa

messages.subject: Re: Simulating leaf temperature in NicheMapR (microclimate and ectotherm parameters)
messages.subject_clean: Simulating leaf temperature in NicheMapR (microclimate and ectotherm parameters)
messages.body_plain:
Hi Lisa,

The microclimate model doesn't give you predictions above the reference height (which is the height at which the meteorological data was measured). But the new function get_profile which I just recently added to NicheMapR can predict to heights above the reference height - just wind speed which keeps increasing logarithmically according to what you put in for the wind shear exponent parameter 'a' (assuming air temperature/relative humidity don't change any more with height above the reference height).

Re the proportionality factor issue, if you're modelling an ellipsoid, you have three axes, 'a', 'b' and 'c'. For a prolate ellipsoid, 'a' is bigger than 'b' and 'c' and is called the 'semi-major axis'. For defining the shape you're assuming a = 1 and represents the length of the leaf, b is the thickness and c is the width, so you'd make b very small to have a thin leaf. In the example in the first appendix in the supporting material for the MEE paper the following is used:
Ww_g <- 1 # wet weight, g
shape <- 2 # 0=plate, 1=cylinder, 2=ellipsoid
shape_b <- 0.0025 # ratio of b axis:a axis for ellipsoid
shape_c <- 0.1176 # ratio of c axis:a axis for ellipsoid

Further down in the example the GEOM.ecto function is used to get some of the absolute geometric consequences of this choice of shape for a 1 g leaf:
GEOM.out <- GEOM_ecto(AMASS = Ww_g/1000, GEOMETRY = shape, SHP = c(1,
shape_b, shape_c), PTCOND = pct_cond/100, PMOUTH = 0, SKINW = 0/100)
w <- GEOM.out$AL/0.7 # leaf width, m
A <- GEOM.out$AREA # total leaf surface area, m2

Hope that helps.
All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: Trouble with nc_to_df subfunction in mcera5 in NicheMapR
messages.subject_clean: Trouble with nc_to_df subfunction in mcera5 in NicheMapR
messages.body_plain:
Hi Morgan,

Yep, mcera5 is my jurisdiction. `lsm` is the land-sea mask, which is used to identify land vs sea pixels; this is then used to perform a correction to capture coastal effects, which ERA5 doesn't handle that well out of the box.

Inspecting your netCDF (era5_2020.nc <http://era5_2020.nc>), indeed the lsm variable is missing – if you queried via mcera5 then I'm not sure how this ended up missing, but perhaps your query was during the flurry of ERA5 moving from ECMWF's old Climate Data Store to the new Climate Data Store, during which some variable names changed, etc.

The best solution is to re-query your ERA5 data now that you have the most updated version of mcera5. You can also download just `lsm` by going to this page <https://48b294cf.streaklinks.com/CLAPOUMfX5TKHvEY9QA3qDXy/https%3A%2F%2Fcds.climate.copernicus.eu%2Fdatasets%2Freanalysis-era5-single-levels%3Ftab%3Ddownload>, checking "land-sea mask" under the "Other" section, checking "netCDF4" under "Data Format", and matching the spatial and temporal extent of your existing netCDF. You could then combine the two netCDFs via NCO, ncdf4, or terra functions.

If it's a pain to re-query your ERA5 data, or you don't care about the coastal correction, here's a quick fix to work with your netCDF as-is without lsm: fork the GitHub repository dklinges9/mcera5 <https://48b294cf.streaklinks.com/CLAPOUEgIGuNBca90Q6TsQ_c/https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fdklinges9%2Fmcera5>, and in internal.R <https://48b294cf.streaklinks.com/CLAPOUEbG-Rb75kMcQh4TMex/https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fdklinges9%2Fmcera5%2Fblob%2Fc47b3d6763620e134db233084c5a13f2e6f427e4%2FR%2Finternal.R%23L182> delete the comma at the end of line 181, and delete lines 182 - 184 and lines 186 - 189. Then install your forked version of the package. This removes the dependency on lsm and micro_era5 should work with your data.

Note that because the new Climate Data Store has a lower API limit than previously, build_request_era5() by default queries ERA5 data by monthly chunks, and then request_era5() by default combines these monthly chunks into an annual file (which is more convenient for eg NicheMapR::micro_era5). This keeps far more ERA5 queries below their API limit (depending on your spatial extent). This lower API limit is a bit of a pain for us, but I'm hoping it's just temporary as ECMWF wraps up their move to the new Climate Data Store.

Feel free to reach out if you have other issues. A lot of mcera5 users reach out directly to me but for cases like this I think it makes sense to parasitize the NicheMapR Google Group given micro_era5()'s reliance on mcera5.

Cheers,
Dave

ᐧ

Hi David and Mike,

Thanks so much for the quick and detailed response! The mcera5 and NicheMapR functions get mixed up in my mind – sorry about that! I’ll go ahead with forking the repo and modifying the code to remove the lsm dependency as you suggested.

If I run into any snags, I’ll reach out again. Thanks again for your help!

Morgan

Dept. of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology

On Fri, Oct 25, 2024 at 10:29 PM David Klinges <dkli...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi Morgan,
>
> Yep, mcera5 is my jurisdiction. `lsm` is the land-sea mask, which is used to identify land vs sea pixels; this is then used to perform a correction to capture coastal effects, which ERA5 doesn't handle that well out of the box.
>
> Inspecting your netCDF (era5_2020.nc <http://era5_2020.nc>), indeed the lsm variable is missing – if you queried via mcera5 then I'm not sure how this ended up missing, but perhaps your query was during the flurry of ERA5 moving from ECMWF's old Climate Data Store to the new Climate Data Store, during which some variable names changed, etc.
>
> The best solution is to re-query your ERA5 data now that you have the most updated version of mcera5. You can also download just `lsm` by going to this page <https://48b294cf.streaklinks.com/CLAPOUMfX5TKHvEY9QA3qDXy/https%3A%2F%2Fcds.climate.copernicus.eu%2Fdatasets%2Freanalysis-era5-single-levels%3Ftab%3Ddownload>, checking "land-sea mask" under the "Other" section, checking "netCDF4" under "Data Format", and matching the spatial and temporal extent of your existing netCDF. You could then combine the two netCDFs via NCO, ncdf4, or terra functions.
>
> If it's a pain to re-query your ERA5 data, or you don't care about the coastal correction, here's a quick fix to work with your netCDF as-is without lsm: fork the GitHub repository dklinges9/mcera5 <https://48b294cf.streaklinks.com/CLAPOUEgIGuNBca90Q6TsQ_c/https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fdklinges9%2Fmcera5>, and in internal.R <https://48b294cf.streaklinks.com/CLAPOUEbG-Rb75kMcQh4TMex/https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fdklinges9%2Fmcera5%2Fblob%2Fc47b3d6763620e134db233084c5a13f2e6f427e4%2FR%2Finternal.R%23L182> delete the comma at the end of line 181, and delete lines 182 - 184 and lines 186 - 189. Then install your forked version of the package. This removes the dependency on lsm and micro_era5 should work with your data.
>
> Note that because the new Climate Data Store has a lower API limit than previously, build_request_era5() by default queries ERA5 data by monthly chunks, and then request_era5() by default combines these monthly chunks into an annual file (which is more convenient for eg NicheMapR::micro_era5). This keeps far more ERA5 queries below their API limit (depending on your spatial extent). This lower API limit is a bit of a pain for us, but I'm hoping it's just temporary as ECMWF wraps up their move to the new Climate Data Store.
>
> Feel free to reach out if you have other issues. A lot of mcera5 users reach out directly to me but for cases like this I think it makes sense to parasitize the NicheMapR Google Group given micro_era5()'s reliance on mcera5.
>
> Cheers,
> Dave
